If the `embed_category` setting was never set, or its value doesn't match a category name, the result is empty, `[0]` raises IndexError and the migration aborts. That is the default case on most sites. The `uncategorized_category_id` lookup on line 15 has the same problem when that setting row is missing (it falls back to a default and may not be stored). db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:22 - Existing hosts are copied unnormalized and interpolated straight into SQL.. The old setting accepted values like `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`; the old specs used exactly these. The migration copies them as-is, along with any trailing `\r` or spaces from `split("\n")`. It skips the model's `before_validation` stripping. `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host`, so these migrated rows never match, and embedding stops working for those sites once the setting is deleted. The value is also interpolated into the SQL string, so a host containing a quote breaks the migration. Strip the scheme, path and whitespace, skip blank entries, and quote the value (e.g. `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`).

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9 - update/destroy raise NoMethodError on an unknown id.. `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for a missing id, for example a host another admin already deleted. `save_host(nil)` and `nil.destroy` then raise and return a 500 error. Use `find` (which gives a 404) or return `render_json_error`/404 when the record is nil. `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` also fails when the `embeddable_host` key is missing.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5 - before_validation crashes when host is nil.. `self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil. That happens with `EmbeddableHost.new` and no host, or a create/update request without `embeddable_host[:host]`. The result is a 500 error instead of a validation error. Guard the block with `if host.present?`, or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:14 - Host lookup fails for mixed-case referers and for hosts saved with a port.. `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the stored column but not the argument. `URI(...).host` keeps the original case, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com/x` is rejected. The validation also explicitly allows a port (`example.com:8080`), which the callback does not strip. `uri.host` never includes the port, so such a record can never match. Downcase the argument, and either strip the port on save or compare it as well.
